spec_match.rationale: Passes SanitizerConfig dictionaries straight to setHTML and the default and strict lanes are genuinely spec-driven on Chromium 157. The custom JSON ships a non-spec key 'removeUnknownMarkup' that is silently ignored, and the lede promises 'deny URL protocols', which SanitizerConfig does not offer.

interactive.rationale: Six examples, a live JSON policy editor and input-driven re-sanitisation update three lanes and the meters on every keystroke.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Three lanes as promised. The 'elements/attributes removed' meters are approximate: attribute removal is counted by positional index between two parses, so the numbers are not trustworthy readouts.

edge_cases.rationale: Good hostile examples (img onerror, iframe, js href, SVG script, form action). Invalid JSON silently becomes {} (equivalent to the default policy) with no error shown. An invalid config such as elements+removeElements throws TypeError, which is swallowed: the lane shows the output of a hand-written JS walker labelled 'custom policy' (verified empty output, no message). The strict lane empties wrapped content (article/h2/ul are dropped together with their children, as the spec intends) without explaining replaceWithChildrenElements.

references.rationale: Cites chromestatus 5814067399491584, but the spec link is the retired WICG draft that now says it 'should be no longer consulted'.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite runs 7/7 PASS on Chromium 157, but five assertions are existence checks and only one (setHTML strips <script>) is behavioural; nothing asserts on* handler removal, javascript: URL removal, that setHTML stays safe even with a permissive custom config, that a malformed SanitizerConfig throws TypeError, or what Document.parseHTML returns.

runtime_evidence.rationale: All six examples, invalid JSON, invalid config and re-sanitise were exercised at both viewports: 0 console errors and 0 failed requests (neutralizePreview stops img src fetches). chrome-devtools-mcp is not available in this environment, so this is NOT DevTools-MCP verification (rule 7b); evidence is Playwright headless Chromium 157.0.8103.78 at 1280x800 and 360x740 DPR3 touch.

telemetry_health.rationale: The shared /public/demo-telemetry.js is injected (runtime/resource errors would be captured) but the page emits no page-specific assertion or interaction events, and /telemetry/demo/events (Basic auth) was not queried in this pass.

design_system.rationale: Uses design-system variables. On desktop the three lanes are cramped and unequal in width (screenshot), with long serialised HTML wrapping awkwardly.

accessibility.rationale: Both textareas have associated <label for>, and the example buttons are native and named. Lane output and meters are not announced, and the JSON parse/config errors that should be surfaced to AT are not surfaced at all. Accessibility tree not inspected with chrome-devtools-mcp (unavailable).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No page-level overflow at 360x740 and the lanes stack, but 6 of 9 controls are under 44px tall on mobile.

openQuestions.title: Surface JSON and SanitizerConfig errors instead of swallowing them
openQuestions.detail: Invalid JSON falls back to {} and a TypeError from setHTML (e.g. elements+removeElements, or a dictionary-shaped attributes) drops into a hand-written JS walker whose output is shown as the 'custom policy'. Show the parse error or the DOMException/TypeError text in the custom lane and render nothing, so users learn the real validation rules.

openQuestions.title: Remove non-spec config keys and claims
openQuestions.detail: Drop 'removeUnknownMarkup' from the default custom JSON. Replace the 'deny URL protocols' promise with what the API actually has: javascript: URL removal by the safe methods, plus the javascriptURLs config key and setJavascriptURLs (feature-detect; absent on Chromium 157).

openQuestions.title: Explain and offer replaceWithChildrenElements in the strict lane
openQuestions.detail: With the legit-article example the strict lane is empty because unlisted wrappers are removed with their children. That is correct per spec but looks broken. Add a toggle or note showing replaceWithChildrenElements:['article','h2','ul','li'] keeping the text.

openQuestions.title: Compute the removal meters from a real diff
openQuestions.detail: Attribute removals are counted by array index between two independently parsed trees, so the readout is approximate. Walk the original and sanitised trees structurally, or label the meter as an estimate.

openQuestions.title: Point the spec reference at WHATWG HTML, not the retired WICG draft
openQuestions.detail: wicg.github.io/sanitizer-api now states the draft 'should be no longer consulted' and that the API was merged into WHATWG HTML. Link the HTML Standard section (Sanitizer, SanitizerConfig, setHTML/parseHTML) from this concept and the feature index.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify with chrome-devtools-mcp and inspect the accessibility tree
openQuestions.detail: This pass used Playwright headless Chromium 157 because chrome-devtools-mcp was unavailable; repeat the control walk and accessibility-tree inspection through the MCP per rule 7b.

guidanceConsulted.query: sanitize untrusted HTML with setHTML instead of innerHTML
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use Element.setHTML()/Document.parseHTML(); a custom Sanitizer can only restrict, never re-allow XSS-unsafe markup; elements not in `elements` are removed with their content (use replaceWithChildrenElements to keep text); move parsed nodes rather than re-serialising through innerHTML.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Used as the grading reference for this critique (review only, no page edits). The page's fallback paths and its unescaped innerHTML log/readout writes run against this guidance; recorded as open questions.

guidanceConsulted.query: form validation error messages for required inputs
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Give clear, accessible error feedback for invalid or missing required input after user interaction.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: invalid input (bad tool name / empty required param / invalid JSON) is silently accepted or ignored; recorded as an open question.

guidanceConsulted.query: live region announcing dynamic log output
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce dynamically changing status/log output through an appropriate live region or <output>, keep native semantics and associated labels for controls.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: the page's changing readouts carry no aria-live/role=status; recorded as an open question.

guidanceConsulted.query: minimum touch target size for buttons on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep touch targets usable (~44px) and content within its space on narrow viewports.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: measured controls below 44px tall at 360x740; recorded under mobile_desktop_parity.

summary: The strongest Sanitizer concept: real setHTML with config dictionaries across three lanes, a clean console and no subresource fetches. Its custom lane hides every configuration error behind a silent {} or JS-walker fallback, and it advertises a non-spec key and a non-existent protocol-deny feature. Verified with Playwright headless Chromium 157, not chrome-devtools-mcp.
